name: limit_detail_outside_the_view
why: ENTRY GT4, the limit of the detail. A circle larger than the view enlarges the VOID, and the enlarged void is still a valid view: it is counted, it has a label, and what reaches the workshop is a box with nothing in it.
_what_changes_compared_to_the_twin: One argument: `radius_mm`. The twin passes it as **8**, which fits on a view about thirty millimetres high on the sheet; here it is **9999**. Same operation, same arguments, same drawing, same part — it is the VALUE that changes, not which argument is passed.
_why_the_twin_passes_radius_mm_even_if_i: Because otherwise they would not be a pair. On 23/9/2026 the pair of the section was born with no argument in common and the bench answered **fake twin: it has not even one argument in common with the refusal, they are two operations that do not talk to each other**. Two calls that share nothing do not show that the check on `radius_mm` works: they show that two different calls do different things.
defect_caught: That the check on the circle disappears. It is a guard that is written once and never seen to fire, so nobody notices the day it stops: from that day the details on the void would come back «done». The message must also carry the numbers — the radius asked for and the size of the view — otherwise whoever reads it does not know by how much they were wrong.

expect.why: same part as the twin up to the step that changes
the part must be on disk before the view names it
the refusal must be the one on the CIRCLE, not the one on «it is not a drawing»
and not the one on «there is nothing to detail» either: the view is there, and it is the circle that is wrong

message_includes: does not fit inside the view
